files.lang.knl:
(* Kanon's built-in bool module, which [use builtin "bool"] reads: here
   bool.knl and bool.kn are copies of it, which [use "bool"] uses, to read and
   to edit. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "bool"
files.bool.knl:
(* The bool module, at the bottom of every language: booleans, equality, [Ite]
   and [Distinct]. See the reference of Kanon for the syntax. *)

node Bool of bool : TBool
notation Bool
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem]
node Or : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem]
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]
node Ite : TBool -> a -> a -> a
node Distinct : a list -> TBool
sort TBool

infix "&&" = And, and_
infix "||" = Or, or_
infix "==" = Eq, eq
prefix "not" = Not, not_

constant true = v_true
constant false = v_false
files.bool.kn:
(* The bool module, at the bottom of every language: booleans, equality, [Ite]
   and [Distinct]. The modules above it add their rules to its rule functions
   with [extend rule], and their literals to [sure_neq] with [extend fn].

   Primitives are implemented by hand by each language, in OCaml and in Lean.
   Oracles have no Lean definition: the Lean model is parameterised by them,
   and the properties that the proofs rely on are stated with the language.
   Here, they are the hash-consing order. *)

(* {1 Primitives} *)

(* Sorts terms along the hash-consing order. *)
oracle sort_by_tag : t list -> t list

prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

(* {1 Helpers} *)

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false

(* whether [a] and [b] surely have different values: the modules above add
   their literals *)
fn sure_neq (a b : t) : bool =
  (not (type_of a = type_of b))
  ||
  match (a, b) with
  | Bool a, Bool b -> not (a = b)
  | _ -> false

fn at_most_one (l : t list) : bool =
  match l with [] | [ _ ] -> true | _ -> false

(* {1 Rules} *)

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | false_: false && _ -> v_false
  | true_: true && x -> x
  | not: p && not p -> v_false
  | and_: (a && _ as x) && a -> x
  | or_: (a || _) && a -> a
  | eq_neq: a == x && a == y when sure_neq x y -> v_false

rule or_ : Or (v1, v2) =
  | true_: true || _ -> v_true
  | false_: false || x -> x
  | not: p || not p -> v_true
  | or_: (a || _ as x) || a -> x
  | and_: (a && _) || a -> a

rule not_ : Not sv =
  | true_: true -> v_false
  | false_: false -> v_true
  | not: not sv -> sv
  | or_: v1 || v2 -> not v1 && not v2
  | and_: v1 && v2 -> not v1 || not v2
  | ite: Ite (g, a, b) -> ite g (not a) (not b)
  | distinct: Distinct [ l; r ] -> l == r

rule ite : Ite (guard, if_, else_) =
  | true_: true, _, _ -> if_
  | false_: false, _, _ -> else_
  | bool: _, true, false -> guard
  | not_bool: _, false, true -> not guard
  | false_then: _, false, _ -> not guard && else_
  | true_then: _, true, _ -> guard || else_
  | false_else: _, _, false -> guard && if_
  | true_else: _, _, true -> not guard || if_
  | not_guard: not g, _, _ -> ite g else_ if_
  | guard_then: g, g, _ -> guard || else_
  | guard_else: g, _, g -> guard && if_
  | ite_then: g, Ite (g, x, _), _ -> ite guard x else_
  | ite_else: g, _, Ite (g, _, y) -> ite guard if_ y
  | and_ite_then: g && _, Ite (g, x, _), _ -> ite guard x else_
  | or_ite_else: g || _, _, Ite (g, _, y) -> ite guard if_ y
  | same: _, x, x -> if_

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: v == v -> v_true
  | bools: Bool b1 == Bool b2 -> of_bool (b1 = b2)
  (* distributing over a shared guard lets the branches cancel pairwise *)
  | ite_ite: Ite (b, l, r) == Ite (b, l', r') -> ite b (l == l') (r == r')
  | false_: false == x -> not x
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | nots: not b == not c -> b == c

(* The equality of terms that may have different sorts, false when they do:
   [@untyped], so its operands are not asserted to have the same sort. *)
rule eq_untyped : Eq (v1, v2) [@untyped] =
  | ill_typed: _ when not (type_of v1 = type_of v2) -> v_false
  | typed: _ -> v1 == v2

(* [distinct_check_one a rest] and [distinct_check l] go through the pairs of
   elements in order, and stop at the first pair that is equal ([Some false])
   or not surely different ([None]). *)
fn distinct_check_one (a : t) (rest : t list) : bool option =
  match rest with
  | [] -> Some true
  | b :: rest ->
      if a = b then Some false
      else if sure_neq a b then distinct_check_one a rest
      else None

fn distinct_check (l : t list) : bool option =
  match l with
  | [] -> Some true
  | a :: rest -> (
      match distinct_check_one a rest with
      | Some true -> distinct_check rest
      | r -> r)

rule distinct : Distinct l =
  | small: _ when at_most_one l -> v_true
  | distinct: _ when distinct_check l = Some true -> v_true
  | not_distinct: _ when distinct_check l = Some false -> v_false
  | default: _ -> Distinct (sort_by_tag l)

files.lang.knl:
(* An example language made of Kanon's bool module alone (modules/bool.kn[l],
   built into kanon, use builtin "bool"), and of variables: Kanon generates the types of
   its terms from these nodes. Its Lean model is in lean/; [kanon ocaml-types]
   and [kanon ocaml] generate its OCaml types and rules, with the primitives of
   the module [Prims]. *)

[@@@lean_root "BoolExample"]
[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use builtin "bool"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "Int"] [@noeq]

node Var of var

(* An example language of integers and of arrays of integers: it shows the
   built-in immutable arrays, whose type [int array] is the argument of a node,
   and which rules build, read and update. Its OCaml is tested in test/ocaml,
   and its Lean model is in lean/. *)

[@@@lean_root "ArraysExample"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "vec"
files.vec.knl:
(* The vec module: integers, and arrays of integers. *)

node Int of int : TInt
notation Int
node Vec of int array : TVec

(** The number of elements of an array. *)
node Len : TVec -> TInt

(** The element at an index, which must be in bounds. *)
node Get : TVec -> TInt -> TInt

(** The array with the element at an index replaced: a copy. *)
node Set : TVec -> TInt -> TInt -> TVec

sort TInt
sort TVec
files.vec.kn:
(* The rules of the vec module. *)

fn in_bounds (a : int array) (i : int) : bool = 0 <= i && i < array_length a

rule len : Len v =
  | lit: Vec a -> Int (array_length a)

rule get : Get (v, i) =
  | lit: Vec a, #k when in_bounds a k -> Int (array_get a k)
  | set_same: Set (_, j, x), k when j = k -> x

rule set : Set (v, i, x) =
  | lit: Vec a, #k, #y when in_bounds a k -> Vec (array_set a k y)

(* arrays are compared structurally *)
fn same (a b : int array) : bool = a = b

(* the conversions between lists and arrays *)
fn of_list (l : int list) : t = Vec (array_of_list l)

fn elements (v : t) : int list =
  match v with
  | Vec a -> array_to_list a
  | _ -> []

files.lang.knl:
(* A tiny language to show the generated traversals: nodes whose children are
   in a list, an array, an option of a tuple, and a record, over two modules.
   Its OCaml is compiled and run in test/ocaml. *)

[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]
[@@@traversals]

use "term"
use "ext"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"]

(** A variable: it has no typing, so a traversal rebuilds it at the sort of the
    term that it replaces (it has no children, so it never does). *)
node Var of var
files.term.knl:
(* The module of the terms: integers, a sum, and nodes with children of every
   shape. *)

sort TInt
sort TBlock
sort TVec
(** The sort of a tuple, over the sorts of its elements. *)
sort TTuple of ty list

(** Something with children in its fields, whose type is a record. *)
type block = { owner : var; offset : t; size : t }

node Int of int : TInt
notation Int

(** The sum: its smart constructor drops a zero. *)
node Add : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@unit 0]

(** A tuple of any number of elements, whose sort is built from theirs. *)
node Tuple of t list (vs) : TTuple (types_of vs)

(** An array of elements. *)
node Vec of t array : TVec

(** An optional pair of an integer and a term, in a tuple in an option. *)
node Opt of (int * t) option : TInt

node Mem of block : TBlock
files.term.kn:
fn types_of (vs : t list) : ty list =
  match vs with
  | [] -> []
  | v :: r -> type_of v :: types_of r

rule add : Add (v1, v2)
files.ext.knl:
(* A module that adds a node: the traversals have its case without a line more. *)

node Neg : TInt -> TInt [@invol]

files.lang.knl:
(* A small value language: booleans and mathematical integers, in one module.
   Kanon generates the types of its terms from its nodes: its OCaml types are
   those of [kanon ocaml-types], in the module [Tiny_types], and its
   primitives are in the module [Tiny_prims]. Its rules are in rules.kn. *)

[@@@ocaml_types "Tiny_types"]
[@@@ocaml_prims "Tiny_prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Tiny_rules"]

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"] [@noeq] [@equal "String.equal"]
  [@hash "Hashtbl.hash"]

(* types of the module Tiny_base, which ocaml-types re-exports *)
type checked [@ocaml "Tiny_base.checked"] = { signed : bool; unsigned : bool }
type rounding [@ocaml "Tiny_base.rounding"] = Nearest | Zero

node Var of var
node Bool of bool
node Int of int : TInt
notation Bool
notation Int
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@fold Rules.add] [@unit 0]
node Times : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 1] [@zero 0]
node Lt : TInt -> TInt -> TBool [@fold Rules.lt]
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]
sort TBool
sort TInt

infix "&&" = And, Rules.and_
infix "+" = Plus, Rules.plus
infix "*" = Times, Rules.times
infix "<" = Lt, Rules.lt_
infix "==" = Eq, Rules.eq
prefix "not" = Not, Rules.not_

constant false = Rules.v_false
files.rules.kn:
prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y
fn lt (x y : int) : bool = x < y

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2)
rule times : Times (v1, v2)
rule lt_ : Lt (v1, v2)

rule not_ : Not v =
  | lit: true -> v_false
  | not_not: not x -> x

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> v_false

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> v_true
  | lits: Int x == Int y -> of_bool (x = y)

(* a parameter of a sort, asserted on entry *)
fn is_zero (v : TInt) : bool =
  match v with
  | 0 -> true
  | _ -> false

(* a node built at a sort *)
fn zero : t = (Int 0 : TInt)

files.lang.knl:
(* A new language, on top of Kanon's bool module: declare its nodes here, and
   write its rules in rules.kn. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use builtin "bool"
use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "Int"]

node Var of var

node Xor : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@unit false]
files.rules.kn:
rule xor : Xor (v1, v2) =
  | same: x, x -> Bool.v_false
  | true_: true, x -> not x

(* A tiny value language: booleans and integers. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"]

(** A variable. *)
node Var of var
(** A boolean literal. *)
node Bool of bool : TBool
(** An integer literal. *)
node Int of int : TInt
(** Negation. *)
node Not : TBool -> TBool [@invol] [@fold Rules.negb]
(** Conjunction. *)
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
(** The sum of two integers. *)
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 0] [@fold Rules.add]
(** Equality of two terms of any sort. *)

(** The sort of integers. *)
sort TInt

infix "+" = Plus, Rules.plus
infix "==" = Eq, Rules.eq
prefix "not" = Not, Rules.not_
files.rules.kn:
(** Whether a variable is surely a natural number. *)
prim var_is_nat : var -> bool

(* Helpers *)
fn negb (b : bool) : bool = not b
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y

(** Whether a term is surely a natural number. *)
fn is_nat (v : t) : bool =
  match v with
  | Int n -> n >= 0
  | Var x -> var_is_nat x
  | l + r -> is_nat l && is_nat r
  | _ -> false

(** A size estimate, for the OCaml code around the simplifier: not modelled in Lean. *)
fn cost (v : t) : int [@no_lean] =
  match v with
  | l + r -> cost l + cost r + 1
  | _ -> 1

(* Rule functions: the rules derived from the laws of their spec come first,
   then these. *)

rule not_ : Not v

(** Conjunction. *)
rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> Bool false

(** Sum: adjacent literals are added. *)
rule plus : Plus (v1, v2) =
  | assoc: (x + #a) + #b -> x + Int (a + b)

(** Equality: literals are compared, and a negative literal differs from a natural number. *)
rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> Bool true
  | lits: Int x == Int y -> Bool (x = y)
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | neg: Int x == y when x < 0 && is_nat y -> Bool false

files.lang.knl:
(* The language: Kanon's bool module, a module of integers, and variables. *)

[@@@lean_root "IntsExample"]
[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use builtin "bool"
use "int"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"]

node Var of var
files.int.knl:
(* The int module: integers, their sum and their order. *)

node Int of int : TInt
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 0] [@fold add]
node Lt : TInt -> TInt -> TBool

sort TInt

notation Int

infix "+" = Plus, plus
infix "lt" = Lt, int_lt
files.int.kn:
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2)

rule int_lt : Lt (v1, v2) =
  | lits: #x lt #y -> Bool.of_bool (x < y)
  | same: x lt x -> Bool.v_false

(* The rules of the bool module, extended to integers *)

extend rule Bool.eq before same =
  | ints: Int x == Int y -> Bool.of_bool (x = y)

extend fn Bool.sure_neq =
  | Int x, Int y -> not (x = y)

files.lang.knl:
(* A language with a subsort: the divisor of a division is not zero. *)

[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "int"
files.int.knl:
(* The int module, with a subsort: what only Lean checks of a term. *)

(** The sort of integers. *)
sort TInt
(** The integers that are not zero. In Lean, `Nonzero`, which is written by hand. *)
subsort TNonzero : TInt [@lean "Nonzero"]

(** An integer literal. *)
node Int of int : TInt
(** The sum of two integers. *)
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 0] [@fold add]
(** The quotient: the divisor is known to be non-zero. *)
node Div : TInt -> TNonzero -> TInt
(** The square of an integer plus one, which is not zero. *)
node Sq1 : TInt -> TNonzero

notation Int

infix "+" = Plus, plus
infix "/" = Div, div
files.int.kn:
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2)

rule div : Div (v1, v2) =
  | self: x / y when x = y -> Int 1

rule sq1 : Sq1 v

files.lang.knl:

[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "int"
files.int.knl:

sort TInt
(** The integers that are not zero. *)
subsort TNonzero : TInt
(** The sort of the results of a comparison. *)
sort TBool

(** An integer literal. *)
node Int of int : TInt
(** The sum of two integers. *)
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 0] [@fold add]
(** The quotient: the divisor is known to be non-zero. *)
node Div : TInt -> TNonzero -> TInt

(** The order on integers. *)
node Lt : TInt -> TInt -> TBool

notation Int

infix "+" = Plus, plus
infix "lt" = Lt, int_lt
files.int.kn:
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y

(** A helper whose result is annotated with its sort: it is typed too. *)
fn double (v : TInt) : TInt = plus v v

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2)
rule div : Div (v1, v2)
rule int_lt : Lt (v1, v2)
